query: How did Bun port 530,000 lines of Zig to Rust in 11 days using a Claude Code agent harness? Cover the harness design: git worktree sharding across parallel dynamic workflows, the PORTING.md rule file and LIFETIMES.tsv lifetime analysis artifact, separating implementer agents from adversarial reviewer agents with isolated context, turning 16,000 compile errors into a work queue, and the validation layers (test suite, security review, fuzzing) beyond test coverage.

facts.desc: Verified: 'Excluding comments, Bun is 535,496 lines of Zig.' (530k is the rounded query figure). https://bun.com/blog/bun-in-rust
Verified: 'about 50 dynamic workflows in Claude Code run continuously over the course of 11 days' (May 3 -> merged May 14, 2026). https://bun.com/blog/bun-in-rust
Verified: 'I split it into just 4 workflow shards each with their own worktree (4 worktrees total), each running 16 claudes'. https://bun.com/blog/bun-in-rust
Verified: 'Claude serialized this discussion into a PORTING.md document' — the porting rule file every ported file had to match. https://bun.com/blog/bun-in-rust
Verified: ports had to match 'the PORTING.md and LIFETIMES.tsv' lifetime-analysis table. https://bun.com/blog/bun-in-rust
Verified: '1 implementer, 2 or more adversarial reviewers per implementer... The implementer doesn't review. The reviewer doesn't implement.' https://bun.com/blog/bun-in-rust
Verified: 'Fixing the cyclical dependencies revealed about 16,000 compiler errors', written by cargo check to a file and divvied up as a work queue. https://bun.com/blog/bun-in-rust
Verified: '24/7 coverage-guided fuzzing of every parser in Bun' plus Fuzzilli for runtime APIs. https://bun.com/blog/bun-in-rust
Verified: 'we've completed 11 rounds of security review from Claude Code Security and addressed the findings'. https://bun.com/blog/bun-in-rust
Verified: 64 Claudes = 16 per worktree x 4 worktrees ('each running 16 claudes'; 'not a crazy number for 64 claudes at once'). https://bun.com/blog/bun-in-rust

traps.desc: Wrong language pair: the port is Zig->Rust (Jarred's earlier esbuild history was Go->Zig, never Go->Rust). https://bun.com/blog/bun-in-rust
Order-of-magnitude-low line count; the real figure is 535,496 lines of Zig. https://bun.com/blog/bun-in-rust
Order-of-magnitude-high line count; the real figure is 535,496 lines of Zig. https://bun.com/blog/bun-in-rust
Wrong duration unit: the port took 11 days, not weeks or months. https://bun.com/blog/bun-in-rust
The port was agent-driven ('at peak Claude wrote about 1,300 lines of code per minute'), not manual. Past-tense assertion form avoids matching negations like 'instead of manually porting'.
It was ~50 dynamic workflows / 64 parallel Claudes, not a single agent. https://bun.com/blog/bun-in-rust

contested.desc: Primary source counts 535,496 lines of Zig excluding comments (https://bun.com/blog/bun-in-rust); press coverage reports ~960,000-1,009,257 total migrated lines (aiweekly.co, LinkedIn commentary). A balanced report cites both scopes.

Zig's creator publicly called the rewrite 'unreviewed slop' (https://www.theregister.com/devops/2026/07/14/zig-creator-calls-buns-claude-rust-rewrite-unreviewed-slop/5270743), while Bun states every line was reviewed by two separate adversarial reviewers before committing (https://bun.com/blog/bun-in-rust).
